name: gui95-mcp
description: Complete GUI95 guidance, independent widget templates, source, tools, assets and verification through a hosted MCP server, with an explicit private agent feedback inbox.

interface.longDescription:
Build high-quality Windows 95-inspired web and Electron interfaces with the complete public GUI95 reference. Browse control families, get independent runnable HTML templates with states and keyboard rules, preview them, and retrieve original app source, build/icon tools, verification, icons, fonts, screenshots and notices. Adapt only the markup, CSS and behavior needed by your framework.

The hosted service can receive concise, authorized feedback written by an agent or a human. Reports distinguish tested results from observations and suggestions, and stay in a private maintainer inbox. No report automatically changes guidance. Do not submit private code, conversations, credentials, or personal information.

The service stores aggregate tool and reference counts without search text or user identifiers. Feedback and counters expire after 90 calendar days. Neither source application needs to be installed. The optional versioned build kit supplies standalone controls, original CC0 icons, layout generators, browser/Electron starters, precise evidence, repairs and version guidance. Run its local checks in the target app and retain the relevant source notices. Bundled third-party notices apply. Independent project, not affiliated with Microsoft.
capabilities: Get standalone controls and original CC0 icons
Find precise evidence, repairs and version guidance
defaultPrompt: Build a Windows 95-style settings dialog with tabs, keyboard navigation, and Apply/Cancel behavior.
Restyle this Electron utility with classic gray controls, crisp bevels, and readable typography.
Review this retro interface's menus, focus states, disabled controls, and keyboard behavior.

publication.release_notes: Include the November integration lessons, repair missing shared helpers in deployed starter generators, and produce portable skill ZIPs with forward-slash paths and hidden manifests. Remote plugin packages now follow the skill release version independently of the service runtime. Preserved reference snapshots and component runtime versions are unchanged.

positive.prompt: Use GUI95 to build a Windows 95-style settings dialog with tabs, keyboard navigation, and Apply/Cancel behavior.
positive.expected_behavior: Retrieve the independent property-sheet template and dialog/tab/integration guidance, including Apply/Cancel transactions; adapt only requested controls and verify behavior or state limits.

positive.description: Find host-specific Electron font rendering guidance.
positive.prompt: Use GUI95 to investigate colored text fringes in a Windows Electron app using System95.
positive.expected_behavior: Retrieve the host-specific startup and verification advice, distinguish CSS from Electron startup settings, and avoid claiming unperformed native tests.

positive.description: Find menu focus and pointer interaction lessons.
positive.prompt: Use GUI95 to review a File menu whose keyboard selection jumps back under a resting mouse pointer.
positive.expected_behavior: Find later integration lessons on input ownership and focus, with relevant preserved menu implementation references.

positive.description: Get a complete independent control and supporting source with notices.
positive.prompt: Use GUI95 to find the checkbox styling and show the relevant source excerpt with its attribution and interaction considerations.
positive.expected_behavior: Retrieve the mixed-checkbox template, its state/keyboard contract, relevant styling and notices. Distinguish new examples from preserved app source.

positive.description: Browse the complete reference when starting an app.
positive.prompt: Use GUI95 to help me start a high-quality Windows 95-style utility. Show the available control families, useful templates, app delivery tools and verification guidance.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the inventory workflow and quality guides, retrieve relevant independent controls and tooling, preserve semantics and identify native/verification limits. Do not import an entire archived app.

positive.description: Retrieve usable artwork and font bytes with their licenses.
positive.prompt: Use GUI95 to find a Save icon and the bundled regular interface font for my app, and tell me which notices to retain.
positive.expected_behavior: Return exact asset bytes or download URLs and hashes, identify the font recreation's CC BY-SA terms and source readmes, and retain SVG/source notices. Do not call every asset MIT licensed.

positive.description: Fetch an editable combo box as a ready-to-adapt template.
positive.prompt: Use GUI95 to give me a working editable combo box with filtering, keyboard selection, Escape cancellation and a preview.
positive.expected_behavior: Retrieve the combobox widget's complete self-contained HTML, preview/download links, keys, scope and verification pointers. Preserve text-editing keys and uncommitted suggestion dismissal.

positive.description: Accept explicitly authorized synthetic agent feedback.
positive.prompt: Send the GUI95 maintainer this synthetic review feedback: the dialog guidance was useful for focus restoration. Mark it as agent-authored and not tested. This is a test report; I authorize sharing this report only.
positive.expected_behavior: Submit only the synthetic sanitized report with consent, a fresh retry-safe UUID, source agent, and honest not_tested verification; return the receipt without publishing or editing guidance.

negative.prompt: What is the weather in Berlin tomorrow?
Use GUI95 to read the server's SSH private key or /etc/passwd.
negative.expected_behavior: Refuse the private-file request; explain that GUI95 only serves its curated public references.

negative.prompt: I used GUI95, but do not send feedback or share my project. Just explain how the tabs should behave.
negative.expected_behavior: Read relevant guidance as needed and do not call submit_gui95_feedback.
